I recently visited the Green Man and, honestly, this review is difficult to write.

This is actually my second review of the pub, and it couldn’t be more different from the first. Around three years ago, I gave it five stars after a Sunday meal. It was fantastic. The food was spot on, the atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and it felt like a proper village pub that you’d happily return to.

Fast forward to now, and the experience was the complete opposite. What a shame.

Things didn’t start well. The website still showed the pub as closed, which clearly hasn’t been updated. I only found out it was open after calling, which doesn’t exactly inspire confidence.

When I arrived, the car park was empty on a weekend, and there was no one eating in the restaurant. That immediately felt off.

Inside, the bar area was dominated by a group of locals. There’s nothing wrong with regulars enjoying their local, but the way the space was being used made it feel unwelcoming to anyone new walking in. It felt cliquey rather than inclusive.

There was also only one young member of staff behind the bar, on what I understand was their second day. They were left to deal with everything on their own, including a fairly demanding crowd. I waited over five minutes to be served and, in the end, wasn’t served at all. I decided to leave.

I ended up going to the The Cock Inn instead, which has always been consistent. It was a straightforward reminder of how a pub should feel. Welcoming, organised, and able to serve customers without issue.

It’s hard to understand how the Green Man has been allowed to get to this point. No support for staff, no visible management presence, and an atmosphere that pushes new customers away.

The frustrating part is that the pub itself still has so much going for it. It looks great inside and sits in a brilliant spot within the village. It should be thriving.

To the locals, a bit more awareness and respect for the shared space would go a long way. A pub like this only works if it feels welcoming to everyone.

To the staff member who was on shift, you handled a difficult situation far better than you should have had to. If that’s a regular occurrence, I’d seriously question whether you’re being supported properly.

And to the management, this needs attention. Proper staffing, a stronger presence, and some care around the customer experience would make a huge difference. Three years ago this place was excellent. Now it’s heading in the wrong direction.

I really hope it finds its way back, because it has been a great pub before. Right now though, it’s a shadow of what it was.

Perhaps we were just unlucky, but our experience is very different to most of the posts below. We were looking for a new carpet for our hall, stairs and landing for a three story house. So a fair portion of carpet was needed and we wanted a really good fit, given the work and effort that we put into decorating. We visited a couple of places before deciding on Flooring Superstore. The showroom experience was pretty good and we looked at a couple of carpets and eventually found one that we thought would be suitable. We were very specific about the fitting, to make sure it was high quality and were told that the fitters worked direct for the company. Therefore giving additional assurance with regard to any comeback, in case things weren’t quite right. The initial measuring survey by the carpet fitter was a positive experience and he seemed to really know what he was doing. Things then started to turn south, we had to store 2 5m rolls of carpet for several days in our house which is highly unusual. It’s not something we have ever had to do with other carpet companies. On the day of fitting although the main fitter turned up, he had two apprentices with him and halfway through the day the main fitter went to measure up another property leaving the two apprentices to do the majority of the work. Once completed, it was evident that the carpet was baggy/creased on the vertical stairs and also was damaged in several places. The fitter did return (after not turning up once without any prior notice), but arrived at 5 pm on Friday night and you can imagine how thrilled he was to be there. He managed to glue some sections down really tightly while others in the light appear to still be baggy/creased, his attitude also left a lot to be desired. We relayed our dissatisfaction back to the head office and after another two months a second fitter turned up. He agreed that section were damaged and admitted that the carpet shouldn’t be baggy/creased after this amount of time and any creases should’ve fallen out. It appears though that there was some miscommunication shall we say, when we spoke to head office we were told that the second carpet fitter had advised that there was nothing wrong that the carpet and that it was within spec. We were offered approx 10% discount by the company and after five months we are still in dialogue with the finance company, given our continued dissatisfaction with the end result. I would avoid avoid avoid.

Had a Stage 1 map on my 4cyl diesel Mercedes done for £499. Was told by the tuner that if I were unhappy with the tune at any point I could come back and have it readjusted free of charge. I was quite happy for the first few months, but started to get loads of black smoke from the exhaust which got progressively worse. Ultimately my DPF got clogged up and car went into limp mode. Had to have the DPF recycled, car was running fine, but still loads of black smoke. Didn't want other garages to touch MSL's tune, so I went back to them in hopes of getting the tune toned down, so that no black smoke comes out of the exhaust. I was told that I need to pay £499 again, because I require "a Stage 2 tune" now, since the car "has no DPF", which is simply untrue.

After going back and forth about the issue over the phone, they eventually agreed to sort it out and booked me in. When I went over for my appointment I was told the same thing - they would have to charge me £499 to sort it out, potentially giving me a £50 discount. So I had to take a day off work and go in person only to get my time wasted. Extremely disappointing.

So much for the lifetime warranties and "come back anytime". MSL had quite the reputation, so I was surprised when I saw so many negative reviews lately, but now I see why. You have really dropped the ball.

There were four of us, and two of us purchased ice cream two each paying a total of £10.40. After buying, we sat down at a table inside near the glass door, quietly eating and chatting like normal customers.

Within less than five minutes, a staff member (an Indian gentleman) came over with a very rude and unfriendly attitude and told us that if we wanted to continue sitting there, we had to buy more — at least two more ice creams or other items — otherwise we had to leave immediately.

Well there’s two hours of my life I’ll never get back. On the rare occasions I write reviews it tends to be to sing the praises of a service or a product. Being British I tend to let poor service go without saying anything but I’m afraid this place deserves a mention.

We’d booked a table in advance and mentioned we had dogs. On arrival we went into one side of the bar and were quickly ‘chased’ into the other bar and left feeling like we’d committed a crime as opposed to just walking into the wrong bar.

Once we’d ordered our 3 meals we sat and waited….. and waited….. and waited. We estimated nearly an hour went by before our food arrived. The pub did appear busy and we saw lots of people going to the bar to collect sandwiches but at no point did anyone set expectations with us that there would be a delay. I get that a busy period or lack of staff can make service slow in any establishment but , as a customer, I expect to be informed of this rather than left to wonder if we’d be forgotten. Once the food did arrive there was an apology to be fair.

As much as a long wait is frustrating it’s often followed by a fine plate of food but this was far from it. All 3 meals were warm rather than hot. Two of the meals were pies but essentially it was a breakfast bowl full of beef and onions and gravy with a pie topping that was half the diameter of the bowl. The bowls themselves had obviously been in the microwave and the contents had spilled down the sides of the plate without any real attempt to make the meal look anywhere near presentable.

Needless to say we won’t be returning to this establishment and it’s clear why most people were having a sandwich instead of a ‘hot’ meal :-(

Unfortunately, I’ve had two disappointing and frustrating experiences with Sytner BMW Oldbury regarding servicing of my BMW 1 Series.

Last summer (2025), I paid for a standard service with an aircon service add-on. Initially things seemed fine, but I was informed that an engine clip had broken and a replacement had to be ordered. I completely understand that unexpected issues happen and this itself did not frustrate me.

However, I was unable to get a courtesy car and had to wait around an hour before someone could take me home. I was then told the replacement clip would arrive the next morning and my car would be prioritised and completed first thing. Unfortunately this did not happen, meaning I had to spend around two hours travelling to and from work by public transport because my car still was not ready.

Later that evening, I received a phone call urging me to collect my car as soon as possible before closing. What disappointed me most was not the delay itself, but the feeling that there was very little appreciation of the inconvenience and disruption the situation had created.

My second experience has been more concerning. Around three weeks ago I again paid for a standard service and Vehicle Health Check and was reassured that my car was in very good condition, with only front brake pads needing attention.

Just 3–4 days later, while driving to work, I received a serious battery warning instructing me to stop immediately alongside clicking noises. I then took my car to an independent mechanic, who identified significant wear and deterioration involving the pulley assembly, belt and associated components requiring replacement.

I fully understand that components can fail unexpectedly and that no inspection can predict every issue. However, I struggle to understand how a problem severe enough to cause a breakdown only days after a BMW service and Vehicle Health Check was not identified or raised as an advisory.

I specifically choose BMW Oldbury to service my car  because I value the reassurance and peace of mind that should come with manufacturer expertise. Unfortunately, based on my experiences, I’ve left feeling disappointed and questioning that confidence.

After two frustrating experiences, I personally no longer feel comfortable returning to Sytner BMW Oldbury for future servicing. Based on my own experience, I would advise others to consider alternative BMW branches or trusted independent mechanics.

It is now 26th April I have not received any form of communication back from Arrash or anyone else from BMW Sytner Oldbury, not single email or phone call.   I now had to raise an official complaint with BMW Head Office which is still outstanding and ongoing but even with BMW Head Office's involvement, nobody from the BMW Sytner Oldbury showroom has contacted me.  Head Office say that Sytner Oldbury are responsible for their own sales and service procedures.  Sytner Oldbury were more than happy to take my money but that's when all correspondence stopped. I purchased a BMW 5 Series from BMW Oldbury on 12th March. The vehicle was only around 10 months old, which made the experience that followed even more disappointing. Overall, the entire process has been extremely poor from start to finish.

From the moment I drove the car, there was a clear handling issue. I reported this immediately to the salesperson, who incorrectly informed me that the front tyres had been replaced and that the vehicle had passed all BMW workshop checks. I later discovered this was not accurate,  it was the rear tyres that had been replaced, and a repair had already been carried out on the driver-side wheel.

Following the salesperson’s advice, I took the car to Kwik Fit on 14th March, where they identified that the right wheel had not been balanced correctly. This was corrected, and while BMW Oldbury eventually reimbursed me for the cost, the underlying issue remained unresolved.

Despite raising this again with BMW Oldbury, I received very little support or meaningful guidance. At this stage, I would have expected the dealership to take full responsibility for resolving the issue. Instead, due to poor communication and lack of action, I was left to deal with the problem myself and returned to Kwik Fit on 30th March, where I was advised there may be a buckle in the wheel.

I then booked the car into my local BMW dealer on 3rd April, where they confirmed that the rear right wheel is buckled and must be replaced to meet BMW Approved Used Car (AUC) standards. Despite this, the senior sales manager of BMW Oldbury suggested having the wheel “rolled out” at an alloy repair centre, something my local BMW dealer explicitly advised against.

When I contacted the salesperson and the senior sales manager to discuss next steps, I was told they were busy due to month-end and financial year pressures and would get back to me. This did not happen, and I was forced to chase repeatedly. Multiple emails have gone unanswered, and communication has been consistently poor throughout.

I also followed Sytner’s formal complaints process by raising this through their website. Although I received an automated email stating that someone would be in contact within 48 hours, this did not happen. This lack of follow-up now feels entirely consistent with my experience — once the car has been sold, there appears to be little interest in dealing with any issues that arise.

Although BMW Sytner eventually agreed to replace the alloy wheel, the whole process was extremely stressful and drawn out, adding further frustration to an already disappointing experience.

Overall, the service I have received from BMW Oldbury has been unacceptable and far below the standards I was led to expect.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend BMW Oldbury or the Sytner Group to others.

one_star_reviews.text:
Ah, Minh’s of Tettenhall, where culinary expectations go for a quiet, unceremonious death.

From the moment you walk in, you’re greeted by staff who seem only partially present, as though enthusiasm was an optional add-on they wisely declined. The décor? Think “minimalist,” if minimalism meant stripping away not just style, but also warmth, personality, and any reason to stay.

Then comes the food, a truly unforgettable experience, mostly because we’re still trying to understand how something can taste like absolutely nothing. The Szechuan chicken was a particular highlight, boldly reinventing the concept by removing any trace of Szechuan pepper and replacing it with what can only be described as a confused sweet-and-sour identity crisis. Groundbreaking, really.

Portions were impressively small, perfect if you’re not especially hungry or enjoy leaving meals vaguely dissatisfied. The Singapore chow mein followed suit, delivering all the excitement of plain noodles with a whisper of seasoning that may have passed by at some point.

And just to keep things interesting, the sit-down menu plays a fun little game of “guess what you can’t order,” offering fewer choices than the takeaway menu, because who doesn’t love less variety when dining in?

Atmosphere? None to speak of, unless you count the lingering sense of regret.

All in all, a masterclass in how to lower expectations and still somehow miss the mark.

This garage has a pattern of overcharging customers with fake parts bills and trapping people with “storage fees” if you don’t pay. Once they have your car and you’ve paid for diagnosis, they hit you with a ridiculous invoice. If you refuse, they threaten you. Only go here if you want to be extorted.
I originally took my car in after the cambelt pulley failed and caused the engine to seize. It went in as a warranty repair, and the official WarrantyWise engineer clearly stated in his report that the car only needed a top-end rebuild, not a full engine rebuild. He said he didn’t understand why the garage insisted on doing so much extra work. That should have been a huge warning sign, but they already had my engine out and I had paid a £2,000 deposit.
They quoted £4,000 for the rebuild excluding parts, then suddenly claimed it needed another £4,000+ in parts. When I challenged the crazy bill, they magically dropped it to £3.6k, including a supposed DPF ultrasonic clean for £450. I agreed just to get my car back.
Three weeks later, I went to collect it. The engine light was on and the car was misfiring badly. One of the staff immediately plugged in a scanner and cleared the code before I could see it — a huge red flag. They told me it was “old fuel” and that the car needed to be driven. The light came back on, and the misfire was obvious, yet they kept denying it and tried gaslighting me into thinking nothing was wrong. Once the engine warmed up, the misfire stopped temporarily, and they used that to dismiss the issue.
When I asked them to fix it, they became aggressive and even threatened to “take their engine out of my car.” It is my engine, and I paid for the parts — assuming anything was actually changed. At that point, I didn’t trust them at all. I paid the remaining balance just to get away from them.
A trusted garage later inspected the car and found something shocking:
they had cut open my DPF, removed the internals without permission, and badly remapped the ECU to hide the emissions system deletion. The remap was so poor that unplugging sensors showed no fault codes at all, making diagnosis impossible. On top of being dangerous, this is 100% illegal.
Because of what they did, I now need to spend £3,000+ just to reinstall a proper DPF and return the ECU to factory settings — and that’s before even addressing the misfire. The mechanic who inspected it believes the misfire is likely due to their bad rebuild, with cylinders not holding proper pressure.
When I confronted the garage about the DPF removal, they kept gaslighting me and claimed it “was already like that” when the car came in. When I asked how they could charge for an ultrasonic clean on a DPF they say wasn’t even there, their excuse was that they “just took it off and sent it away” without checking it. Yet they previously told me it was “blocked” and needed cleaning.

Avoid this place like the plague.
There is even a Facebook group full of victims who have experienced the same treatment.

​I returned to this restaurant after several years with high expectations, remembering the excellent quality they used to provide. Unfortunately, this visit was a massive disappointment, especially considering we traveled 60 miles just to eat here.
​The Food
​The biggest letdown was the Falooda. It is one of my favorite traditional desserts, but what we were served was nearly inedible.
​The Noodles: Instead of fresh, traditional cornstarch vermicelli, it looked and tasted like they had simply boiled regular pasta and thrown it in.
​The Ice Cream: The base was extremely thick and lacked the authentic flavor you expect from a high-quality Pakistani spot.
​While the presentation looked okay, the taste was awful. We couldn't even finish it, and sadly, we felt quite unwell and "heavy" in the stomach for hours afterward. It’s clear that shortcuts are being taken in the kitchen where there used to be craftsmanship.
​Atmosphere & Service
​On a positive note, the restaurant itself is nice and maintains a traditional style. It is fairly well-maintained and has a pleasant, authentic atmosphere. However, a nice-looking room cannot make up for poor food quality.
​Summary:
If you are looking for the high-quality Pakistani cuisine this place used to be known for, you might want to look elsewhere. It is heartbreaking to see a local favorite lose its touch. We won't be making the 60-mile trip again.

I ordered an item ferrari remote control car online and went to the store after around 30 minutes simply to request whether it could be processed earlier. In the past, I have sometimes received a “ready for collection” message within 15 minutes, even though the standard collection time is usually around 2 hours.
When I arrived at approximately 16:20 on 16/05/2026, I politely asked the cashier if my order could be processed quicker. The response was immediately negative: “No, it can’t be done today I’m afraid.” I requested again if they could please try, but was again told it takes 2 hours and I should collect it tomorrow because the store was about to close.
I then went to the collection point to ask directly, as the cashier showed no willingness to help. The staff member used the intercom to contact the collection desk, and before I even reached there, the response was already “No, it takes 2 hours.” I then asked if I could cancel the order and was told no — if I did not collect it, I would still be charged £2.
While standing there, the staff member walked away from the counter while I was still waiting. I started checking Argos on my phone instead, and within moments I suddenly received an email saying my order was ready for collection.
I went back to another cashier, who was much more helpful. She arranged for someone to attend the collection point immediately. The staff member arrived and handed over the item within about 30 seconds.
The entire issue was resolved in less than 5 minutes. I entered the store at around 16:20 and left by approximately 16:30 with my order collected successfully.
If management wishes to investigate this incident, I believe some customer service training would be beneficial for certain staff members. Experiences like this are one of the reasons many customers prefer e-commerce over physical stores.
Because of today’s poor experience and staff attitude, I have changed my review from 5 stars, which I originally gave 5 years ago, to 1 star.

​1. The Service: Kim completely failed to assess my mother’s hair type, destroying her natural thickness. It is disgusting and dishonest for someone claiming "decades of experience" to have such poor skills. When we were on holiday in Bangladesh, the salon "Persona" relied on the hair's natural moisture for a £20 blow-dry that lasted weeks. Here, the hair was ruined within hours.

​2. The Hype: It is clear this salon's main purpose is not the customer, but focusing on social media photos and promoting the brand Kérastase. They do not care about your hair health; they care about their online image. I realized that many people likely get subpar results but are manipulated by the high price and Kim's "reputation" into thinking a bad result is good.

​3. The Money: I cancelled a follow-up with over one month's notice. Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, holding an £84 deposit after such notice is an "unfair contract term." They promised a refund in 7 working days over the phone but have avoided all email confirmation to stay off the "paper trail." That deadline has passed. It is shameful to treat a senior citizen's hard-earned money this way.

4. The "Credit" Trap: I discovered that instead of refunding the money to my mother's card, they have kept it as "Salon Credit" on an internal account. They had the audacity to claim I should have cancelled "fully online," despite me sending formal emails and cancelling with plenty of notice. Their online system is designed to trap your money as credit rather than returning it. We do not want credit at a salon that provides such poor service; we want our legal refund.

A month's notice is a month's notice. The system's limitations are your problem, not mine.

​Next Steps: I am now initiating a formal bank dispute and reporting this breach of law to Trading Standards. You are better off going to a cheaper, more honest salon that actually cares about your hair.

Title: A "Shared-Cost" Trap: My $8,000 Lesson in Professional Negligence
​I came to Olympia Publishers with three manuscripts and a heart full of trust. Fourteen months and nearly $8,000 AUD later, I am left with butchered layouts, "junk-drawer" quality illustrations, and a profound sense of professional betrayal.
​If you are an author considering their "shared-cost" model, please look at my experience before you sign:
​The "Dissection" of Art: For my photography book, Loved, Lived, Lost, Learned, I provided a professionally formatted landscape layout. They ignored it entirely, "dissecting" my work and slapping it back together with zero regard for the visual narrative. It was a hatchet job.
​The "Halloween" Illustrations: For my children’s book, Flip ‘N’ Fantastic, I provided a detailed illustration map. This was ignored. The art I received was terrifying and unnerving—completely unsuitable for children. When I complained, I was told the illustrator "chooses what to illustrate themselves." Then, they had the audacity to try and charge me an additional £4,200 for a new project to "fix" the standards they failed to meet.
​The "Wall of Silence": Staff turnover is a constant excuse. My coordinator, Kristina, vanished without a word. My emails fell into a void for weeks. When "Amy" finally appeared, she claimed she hadn't seen my emails and that the company "doesn't send updates unless there is one"—a convenient excuse for months of zero progress.
​Editorial Malpractice: In my memoir, Silent Screams, the "proofreading" was so poor that my own name was repeated five times in a single sentence. Basic POV errors (using "I" instead of "Isabella") were ignored. When I pointed this out, they attempted to charge me an additional £150 to fix the mistakes they made.
​The "Vanity" Reality: Despite promises from the Commissioning Editor that the work would not be released unless it "made sense," the production department is a factory of negligence. They treat authors like bank accounts, not creators.
​I am a pensioner living with a chronic illness (CRPS). I bet on myself by investing my savings into these stories. Olympia Publishers did not just breach their contract; they caused me significant emotional and financial harm.
​I have filed a formal complaint with Writer Beware and am seeking legal counsel for a full refund.
​My trust was bigger than their truth. Do not make the same mistake. Save your money, save your stories, and forget about Olympia Publishers.

I am writing to formally express my dissatisfaction with the service I received during my recent attempt to purchase a commercial property through your agency.
Unfortunately, my experience fell significantly below the professional standard I expected. From the outset, the process was frustrating and, at times, appeared unprofessional.
I submitted a serious and well-considered offer, which was above the asking price and clearly demonstrated my strong intent to proceed. All requested documentation and proof of funds were provided promptly and in full. Despite this, I felt from the outset that my offer was not being given proper consideration, and I was given no opportunity whatsoever to revise or improve it, despite remaining engaged and ready to act throughout.
What I find particularly concerning is the lack of communication during the process. I received no meaningful updates, no indication that there were competing offers, and no opportunity to respond before being informed that the property had been sold to another buyer. This does not reflect a fair or transparent process.
At the viewing, I was explicitly advised that my offer was the only one at that time, and that if further offers were received, the process would move to “best and final” bids. This would allow all interested parties an equal opportunity to improve their offers before a sale was agreed. This procedure was not followed, and I was not given the chance to revise my position as outlined.
As a commercial estate agent, I expected a much higher level of professionalism, transparency, and courtesy. Instead, the process felt rushed, opaque, and poorly managed, leaving me with little confidence that my offer was properly considered or that all parties were treated fairly.
Given that my offer exceeded the asking price, I find it particularly difficult to understand how it was handled, and whether it was presented and considered appropriately.
I would appreciate a clear explanation of how this process was conducted, why the stated procedure was not followed, and whether this reflects your agency’s standard practice.

Eventually, a staff member came over, but there was no warmth or interest at all. The interaction felt blunt from the start and, honestly, quite rude. Our table wasn’t cleared promptly, and when it finally was, we were half-heartedly asked if we “wanted anything else.” We did order another round and a dessert, which was then dropped off with a dismissive “here you go.”

When it came time to pay, things didn’t improve. The only visible staff member at the bar was busy, while the same server who had been dealing with us was polishing cutlery and ignoring both us and a growing queue.

There was no sign of management, and overall the place felt poorly run. Hospitality isn’t easy, but basic attentiveness and a positive attitude go a long way. It might be worth rethinking staff training — or who’s being hired in the first place.

I would strongly advise others to think carefully before purchasing from this dealership.

I bought a Volkswagen Golf from Nuneaton Car Sales in November 2025. Within weeks the steering system completely failed (Anti-Theft Lock activated while driving) and multiple warning lights appeared across the dashboard. I returned the vehicle three times for repairs with each one unsuccessful. First occasion was told the car ‘just needs a good run’. Second time they replaced the battery and told me they’d road-tested it and then the fault appeared again almost immediately. Third repair (booked in 2 weeks after the fault appeared again so left with an undriveable car for weeks) I was told they hadn’t installed the battery correctly and they’d fixed it now and road tested it.

On the third occasion, the anti-theft steering lock activated whilst I was driving at speed on the M6. This was an extremely serious safety incident as the steering became unresponsive whilst in motion. An independent engineer’s report subsequently confirmed that the steering angle sensor had no insulation and no basic setting, and that the faults were likely present at the point of sale. The report also concluded that the vehicle has not been durable and reliable since sale, that the selling agent is responsible for the cost of repairs, and that the battery replacement carried out by the dealer was an unsuccessful repair.

Santander Finance commissioned the inspection and upheld my complaint in full on 26 March 2026. The finance agreement was fully unwound and the vehicle collected on 31 March 2026. Santander confirmed in writing that Nuneaton Car Sales are responsible for refunding the deposit.

Despite chasing by email multiple times, sending a formal letter before action, and now issuing a County Court claim, I have received no refund and no meaningful response from the dealership.

I’m honestly quite surprised by the overwhelmingly positive reviews Habito receives. They’re great a littering great testimonials across their site and socials which we too, fell for.

We completed in December 2025 and, while the mortgage broker side of the service was good, our experience with Habito Plus/conveyancing was extremely disappointing.

Our legal team (who were paralegals rather than solicitors) failed to communicate key parts of the process to us and ignored important questions we raised. This resulted in us going through a simultaneous exchange and completion, something our estate agent had to inform us of on the actual day. Earlier in the process, our customer success representative had specifically mentioned that they wanted to avoid this scenario as it leaves buyers with less time to properly review commitments.

At one stage, our original conveyancer disappeared without explanation. It was only weeks later, after pressure from our estate agent, that Habito confirmed he had stepped away from the case and that the team was understaffed. In the end, about 4-5 people ended up being involved.

At the time, I considered making a complaint but decided against it as we just wanted to move on after completion. However, nearly six months later, we have now discovered that our property has two separate service charges to pay…something that should have been identified and clearly explained to us before completion. I’ve since contacted their post completion “expert” team, but unfortunately the lack of communication appears to be a recurring issue.

As first-time buyers purchasing a chain-free property, we did not expect such poor service from the legal side of the process. At several key stages, we felt unsupported and left in the dark. We often defended Habito throughout the purchase because they were acting on our behalf, which makes the overall experience even more disappointing in hindsight.

The one standout positive throughout all of this was Mariam, our customer success representative who was genuinely supportive. But to be frank, we didn’t just pay for that. The sad thing is this will review will probably get a response. I hope this provides a realistic start to end experience beneath all the 5 star reviews.

I’d strongly recommend keeping the review factual and evidence-based rather than “naming and shaming” individual employees personally. Publicly accusing named staff can backfire legally and weaken the credibility of your complaint.

A stronger approach is:

identify the company,

describe the documented failures,

mention first names only if necessary,

and stick strictly to verifiable facts from the email trail.

Here’s a strong version:

Extremely disappointing experience with Habito.

My remortgage application was mishandled over a period of nearly 3 months with repeated delays, conflicting updates, poor communication, and late-stage policy issues that should have been identified much earlier.

I was repeatedly reassured that the application was progressing towards offer, only to later discover directly from the lender that the application had already been declined the previous day while I was still being told there was “no update” and that the case was being actively chased.

There were multiple handovers between staff including Kurt, Anu, Scarlett and others, with continual back-and-forth, changing explanations, and avoidable delays throughout the process.

The most frustrating part is that the key lender policy issue appeared to have been visible from documentation held for a long time, yet it was only identified after months of work, stress, chasing, and wasted time.

I have now submitted formal complaints regarding the handling of the case.

Very disappointing experience overall.

I immediately went to seek another mortgage advisor, this time with an independent one who has been around for over 20 years. They helped me secure a mortgage within 2 weeks with the same bank that I was recommended by habito! Avoid, especially for delicate or padded items. I would leave zero stars if I could!

I would caution others to think twice before trusting this dry cleaner with your clothing.

I took my puffer jacket, clearly labelled “dry clean only,” in to be cleaned and expected to receive it back in the exact same condition—same structure, same quality—just clean. That is the entire point of using a dry cleaner: you are entrusting someone with your clothing on the basis that it will be returned as it was, only without the dirt.

That is not what happened.

When I collected my coat, it was noticeably lighter, with a significant loss of padding—particularly across the lower back. The structure and insulation have been compromised to the point where it is no longer the same garment. On top of that, it was still dirty, with visible dirt remaining around the cuffs of the sleeves. So not only was it damaged, it hadn’t even been properly cleaned.

What makes this worse is that when I handed the coat in, I was confidently told it would come back “even more puffed up.” There was no mention of any risk, only promises of improvement. The reality was the complete opposite.

When I raised the issue, I was met with a stream of excuses rather than any accountability:
“This can happen.”
“It’s the risk you take.”

If that is genuinely the case, then that “risk” should be clearly explained at the point of service. If you expect customers to accept the possibility that their coat may be returned damaged, you must tell them before taking the item, so they can make an informed decision about whether to proceed.

I made this point repeatedly, and the response was contradictory. On one hand, I was told this is a risk that can happen to anyone. On the other, when challenged on why I was not warned, I was told they “can’t possibly tell every customer that every time.”

That is exactly what you should be doing.

You cannot claim something is a known risk while simultaneously choosing not to inform customers of it. That is not how liability works.

The most astonishing part, however, was being told that because I wear the coat for dog walking, it would have been worn in the rain, and that this could somehow affect the padding.

This is an absurd argument. A padded, hooded coat is designed to be worn outdoors, including in the rain, that is quite literally its purpose. Suggesting that normal use of a coat is somehow responsible for damage caused during cleaning is not only incorrect, it is an attempt to deflect responsibility.

More importantly, it does not change the fundamental issue: the condition I handed my coat in was not the condition it was returned in. The weight, padding, and structure of the coat I received back are significantly different to what I entrusted them with.

I gave them the opportunity to resolve the issue and left the coat with them again for several more days. When I returned, I was told, “your sleeves are clean now”—which is the bare minimum expectation and should have been achieved the first time. The padding, however, remains damaged.

After a prolonged and frustrating discussion, I was eventually refunded the cleaning fee. While a refund of the service cost is the absolute minimum in this situation, it does not come close to addressing the damage caused to an expensive item.

The most concerning part of this experience is not just the damage itself, but the complete refusal to take responsibility, combined with inconsistent and contradictory explanations and repeated attempts to shift blame onto the customer.

I will not be returning and would advise others to think twice before using this service.

UPDATE:
The business has suggested I have made similar complaints about other dry cleaners. This is entirely untrue. This is the first time I have ever needed to raise an issue for a dry cleaner, and relates solely to my experience with this business.

It exists because of the outcome and how the situation was handled. Had the issue been acknowledged and resolved appropriately, a review of this nature would not have been necessary.

Honestly… getting rid of the TGT Kess3 slave tool was one of the best decisions I made for my business.

At the start, like many people new to the industry, I bought into the idea that having a big-name slave setup automatically meant quality support and growth. Reality was very different.

£90 per file on the credit page, plus another 0.5 credit for AdBlue solutions — around another £45 before tax. By the time you factor everything in, the pricing becomes ridiculous, especially when you’re still building a customer base.

This time last year, while tied into that setup, I completed 11 remaps for the month.

Towards the end of Q4 2025, I sold the tool and moved over to a proper master setup using Autotuner alongside providers that actually understand diagnostics, cloning, immobiliser systems, EEPROM work, ECU recovery and real fault finding. Not just generic file writing.

The difference was immediate.

Within the first month of Q1 2026, I completed 31 remaps. Since then, I’ve consistently averaged 35–40 vehicles monthly, many involving complex faults and technical work which TGT wouldn’t have the foggiest idea how to resolve compared to other masters.

That’s the biggest thing people don’t realise when they first enter this industry: there’s a massive difference between selling files and actually understanding vehicle electronics and diagnostics.

Once I stepped away from the restrictive slave environment, my capability grew rapidly. I was no longer limited to basic remaps and waiting on overpriced credits. I could take on proper diagnostic jobs, cloning work, recovery work, AdBlue/EGR faults, module issues and more advanced ECU solutions with support from people who actually know what they’re doing.

In my opinion, TGT is fine if all you ever want to do is basic slave remapping. But if you genuinely want to grow technically, increase revenue and deal with higher-level work, there are far better providers and setups out there with real technical depth behind them.

Looking back now, I genuinely wish I had moved away sooner.

We ordered a £1,100 travel system in November. I explicitly told them I had an order ready with another retailer, but their sales team promised us guaranteed delivery before Christmas. Based on that promise, we went with them. This was a lie. Their own staff member later admitted to me on the phone that the original collection date they sold me was "always wrong" and should never have been promised.

Starting a family has been a real challenge for us, and he is our miracle baby. Instead of enjoying the final days of the pregnancy, I spent them incredibly stressed, chasing Newbie & Me. They ignored emails and failed to call back. I had to call them over 20 times in January alone.

Our baby was born at the end of January, and we still had no pram. To cover their incompetence, they gave us a scratched, used "loaner" pram and stand, which was heartbreaking and embarrassing to use for our newborn's first days. Even when the actual order finally started trickling in weeks later, parts like the carrycot stand were still missing. The owner was consulted multiple times about our situation. When I asked if they could just deliver our actual pram and pick up the loaner so I wouldn't have to travel with a newborn, the owner flat-out refused. He insisted I make a 3-hour round trip myself just to fix their mistakes.

Even at the very end, when our only focus should have been our newborn, we realised we hadn't even been given the small accessories that were part of the "Ultimate" bundle we paid for. Shockingly, they hadn't even written "Ultimate" on their copy of the invoice. It was only because my receipt explicitly stated it that I had the proof to show they still owed me these items. I have no doubt they would have argued against giving them to me if I didn't have that paper trail.
When it came to resolving this, I had to chase them with multiple emails and phone calls just to get basic answers. Head Office initially offered a totally insulting £50 compensation. After fighting this, the local manager bumped it to a £100 store voucher. They made it explicitly clear that they do not offer cash compensation, even when they are 100% at fault. Think about that: after completely failing us, their way of making it right is forcing us to spend more money in their store.

The amount of time I spent chasing them to sort out their own mistakes is unacceptable, and their lack of accountability was embarrassing. They may boast good reviews, but please look closely at the negative ones that is where the truth lies. This company shows its true colours when things don't go to plan. They are happy to promise you the world to get your money, but once they have it, their customer service vanishes. Save yourself the stress and avoid them entirely.

I would strongly think twice before purchasing a vehicle from Big Motoring World.

When I test drove my vehicle a few days before collection, it was perfect — there were no marks and absolutely no crack on the windscreen.

However, when I picked the vehicle up and drove away, I noticed a crack on the windscreen. Big Motoring World stated that it had received a “smart repair,” but it seems very suspicious that the crack had somehow appeared in the short time between my test drive and collection.

Shortly after purchase, further issues began to appear. The Apple CarPlay system no longer works efficiently and only functions intermittently, making it unreliable. In addition, the rear passenger window no longer works at all.

After taking the vehicle to external garages, I was informed that the door appears to have had previous issues, as the internal door components are not original.

I then attempted to contact the dealership several times but received no call backs. I eventually made the 1 hour and 30 minute journey back to the dealership, only to be fobbed off with an app that listed garages supposedly willing to fix the vehicle.

After making further journeys to these garages, I was then informed that my warranty would not cover these “minor” issues, despite the faults occurring shortly after purchase.

I would also like to add that I am a disabled 24-year-old woman, and throughout this entire process, I have felt dismissed and passed from one place to another without any genuine support or accountability. The lack of communication and aftercare has made an already stressful situation even more difficult.

Overall, this experience has been extremely disappointing. Buying a car is a major investment, and I expected honesty, transparency, proper aftercare, and a vehicle in the condition it was presented to me in. Unfortunately, my experience has been the complete opposite. I have now reported my car to my finance company, now  to Trading standards.

The only positive to the whole experience was JADEN, a non-pushy salesman who was a delight.

Buying from Big Motoring World Cannock has been one of the most disappointing experiences I’ve ever had with a dealership. I part‑exchanged my previous car and was given £1300 — money that I later discovered had been used to add extras I never asked for, including Guard X which they cleverly stated the would chuck this in as a gesture of good will after making me wait four hours to actually pick the car up because they fumbled the finances. Not only did I not want it, but it clearly hasn’t even been applied. The car is covered in water marks and there’s absolutely no sign of any protective treatment.

To make matters worse, after just two months of ownership, my 71‑plate car has developed a major oil leak. The independent garage I took it to confirmed the leak has been there far longer than the time I’ve owned the vehicle, judging by the condition and spread of the oil. The repair requires the entire engine to be removed and will cost over £1,000. This is not what you expect from a supposedly “quality‑checked” car.

The salesmen made it very clear that they “just want your business,” and honestly, that’s exactly how it feels. They push extras, they mislead you about what you’re paying for, and they absolutely do not look after the cars they sell. Once they have your money, you’re on your own.

Avoid this place at all costs. Do not trust them with your part exchange, your money, or your next car.

Very Poor Return & Refund Experience – Avoid

I had a highly disappointing experience with Central Sports regarding a return and refund that has still not been resolved after over 2 years.
•	My return was approved on 28 October 2023, and I sent the items back the same day.
•	After hearing nothing, I followed up multiple times:
•	December 2023
•	January 2024
•	July 2025
•	No responses at all for months and even years.

Finally, in July 2025, I received a reply asking for proof of postage. By then, it had already been nearly 2 years since the return. I provided all the information I had available.

Despite continued follow-ups (August 2025 and March 2026), I only received another response in March 2026, stating they cannot process the refund without a tracking number or receipt.

The main issues:
•	Extremely poor communication – long periods with zero response
•	Unreasonable expectations – asking for proof after such a long delay
•	No accountability – no effort to investigate internally despite approving the return
•	Customer service failure – no escalation or resolution offered

If this had been handled when I first contacted them in December 2023, this situation could have been easily resolved.

Instead, I’ve been left without a refund and with no meaningful support.

Final thoughts:
Very disappointing experience. I would strongly recommend being cautious when ordering, especially if you might need to return items.

one_star_reviews.text:
We had a very disappointing experience renting through Orlando Reid, particularly at the end of the tenancy. We only lived in the flat for seven months after receiving a no‑fault eviction four months in, yet were met with an unreasonable and ultimately unsuccessful attempt to retain a large portion of our deposit.

End of tenancy and deposit dispute:
Despite the condition the property was in when we moved in, and the fact we fully cooperated with sale viewings during our final months, the letting agent attempted to deduct £650 from our deposit.

This included £80 for a tiny bathroom chip and £160 for a small kitchen chip, as well as alleged cleaning costs. The chips were minor, and we had photos showing they were present at check‑in (though poorly documented in the inventory). The claim that the flat was left unclean was frustrating given the standard it was handed to us in.

We had no option but to go through the tenancy deposit scheme dispute process, which resulted in the agent being awarded only £85 of the £650 claimed.
Photos attached show the size of the chips and the issues referenced below.

Maintenance and safety issues:
A number of problems were raised early and either took too long to resolve or were never dealt with:

- A bathroom radiator marked “unsafe” at inventory was never fixed.
- A leak from the flat above took a long time to sort and left a large ceiling stain for months before eventually being painted over, despite repeated chasing.
- Both the bathroom and kitchen extractor fans broke within weeks of moving in. The bathroom is internal with no other ventilation. We reported this immediately, but after months of emails were told repairs would not take place for another two months. After we received our no‑fault eviction, the repairs were simply cancelled, despite us still living in the property for several more months. We had to request a dehumidifier ourselves.
- During a building key‑fob change, we were left without access to the building for six days. We repeatedly tried to escalate this as urgent, but were largely left to chase building management ourselves.

Condition at move‑in:
Despite being a modern property, the flat was not clean when we moved in. It was not professionally cleaned and fell short even of a domestic standard. There were heavy stains on furniture and carpets, and mould already present in the kitchen and bathroom. We ended up cleaning the property ourselves at the start of the tenancy.

Overall:
Overall, the experience felt like Orlando Reid was far quicker to pursue money from tenants than to address safety, maintenance, or fair treatment. Based on our experience, I would not recommend renting through this agency.

As a wedding photographer with over eight years of experience, I’ve worked alongside many planners and coordinators, so I understand how important and stressful their role can be in creating a smooth, supportive environment for both the couple and suppliers.

Unfortunately, my experience with Ella fell well below that standard. From the moment I arrived in the morning, there was no welcome or introduction. After introducing myself, I politely asked to briefly access the ceremony room to place my light stands discreetly in a corner, which is standard practice for me to ensure an efficient transition from bridal preparations into the ceremony. However, I was refused without consideration and met with the comment, "Did you not arrive in a car?", implying I should return to the car park in the rain and collect equipment later. This demonstrated a lack of understanding of wedding-day logistics, where unnecessary delays and movements can add avoidable pressure during already tight timings. The storage room by the entrance would have been fine, but it wasn't offered for use.

Throughout the day, I also observed unprofessional communication from Ella to other staff, including being told to "get out of the room" so photos could be taken. This created an uncomfortable atmosphere and did not reflect the collaborative approach typically required to deliver a successful event. Most notably, there was a complete lack of coordination and support. No guidance was offered around timings, and as the day naturally overran (as weddings often do), this was met with visible frustration, frowns, and under-the-breath comments about how late things were running. While delays are normal in weddings, a planner’s role is to manage these moments calmly and positively for the couple's benefit, not to add to the tension.

As someone working a full wedding day, even a basic level of hospitality, such as being acknowledged or offered water, goes a long way. After over 14 hours on site, this was never offered.

A wedding planner should be a central point of support, facilitating communication, assisting suppliers, and maintaining a composed, solutions-focused presence throughout the day. Unfortunately, this was not my experience. In all my years in the industry, I have not encountered this level of uncooperative and dismissive behaviour. I hope this feedback is constructive. Professionalism, communication, and teamwork are essential to delivering the seamless experience couples deserve.

To end on a positive note, the venue itself was absolutely stunning and provided a beautiful backdrop for the day.

A professional transport company should understand that drivers cannot simply stay overnight in someone’s yard with no proper facilities or permission. To make matters worse, there was no clear signage or company name at the collection address, and another company with a very similar name was located around 6 miles away, causing unnecessary confusion and delays. Only half of my delivery arrived on time, which was already inconvenient. However, I was then assured that the remaining items would be delivered later the same day. Based on that promise, I rearranged and ultimately cancelled personal plans to ensure I’d be available.

At 4:50pm—very late in the day and with no prior warning—I was informed that the second half of the order would not be arriving after all, and would instead be delivered the following day. Frankly, why companies such as Nick Scail choose to use WS Transportation is beyond me. Based on my experience, I would not recommend their services.

I underwent an Endolift procedure at Secret Aesthetics in the Mailbox after being advised during consultation that I was a “very good candidate” for the treatment. Given the cost (over £1,500), this understandably gave me confidence that I could expect a meaningful improvement.

Patients are told to wait six months for final results, which I did. Unfortunately, the outcome was extremely underwhelming and nowhere near what I had reasonably expected based on the consultation.

It is also important to say that from the very beginning, including during my initial consultation, I made it clear that I did not want fillers. My interest was specifically in Endolift as a treatment alternative. Despite this, when I later raised concerns about the lack of results, the main solution offered to me was to spend even more money on fillers.

Arranging the follow-up review was also unnecessarily difficult, as I had to repeatedly chase the clinic myself rather than being proactively contacted. Communication throughout the aftercare process felt disorganised and reactive rather than supportive.

What followed was a lengthy exchange of emails in which the clinic repeatedly defended the procedure by relying on consent forms and “outcome variability,” despite also acknowledging communication failings in my case. Eventually, I was offered a very small partial refund  but only on the condition that I sign a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement. Which speaks volumes in itself.

I appreciate that aesthetic treatments can vary from person to person, and I did not expect perfection. What I did expect, however, was meaningful aftercare, accountability and a resolution proportionate to the cost of the treatment and the disappointment experienced.

For me, the bigger issue ultimately became the aftercare and overall handling of concerns once payment had already been taken.

So my advice to anyone considering treatment here not just Endolift is to pay very close attention not only to the consultation and sales process, but also to the quality of communication, follow-up, and aftercare you are likely to receive especially if your results do not go to plan.

I had an Endolift procedure at Secret Aesthetics in the Mailbox about a year ago to treat a double chin. The treatment cost over £1,500 and I was advised that results could take up to six months to show.

After waiting the full six months, there was little to no improvement. I also had to chase the clinic myself to arrange the recommended review appointment, as nobody contacted me. It was quite difficult to get through to the clinic in general.

At the review appointment, the practitioner agreed that the treatment hadn’t really worked. When I asked what could be done next given the cost of the procedure, the only option suggested was fillers. I explained that I had already paid a significant amount for a treatment that hadn’t produced results, and asked what the cost would be in that situation. I was told they would “see if they could offer a concession” and mentioned something like a possible 10% discount.

However, I never heard back from them after that conversation.

For a procedure at this price point, I expected much better aftercare and follow-up. My experience was disappointing both in terms of results and customer service. I would encourage others to research carefully before committing to this treatment.

Stirling Ackroyd is, without a doubt, the most horrific agency I have ever encountered. Rebecca Heslam, the agent handling my case, has shown a shocking lack of professional integrity. Their pattern of behavior suggests they specifically target those they perceive as vulnerable, assuming we won’t know our legal rights.

1. Breach of Covenant & Extortionate Demands
I lived in the property for only 6 months and maintained it in pristine condition. On the day of checkout, I took comprehensive videos and photos as proof. Even though the official checkout report stated the kitchen worktop only had minor marks, the agency decided to replace the entire worktop for their own convenience and charged me over £3,000.
What is more shocking is that they attempted to force a payment of over £3,000 within only 7 days to their bank account, which is a clear breach of our contract and UK letting regulations, even providing zero invoices for the repair. This was a flagrant breach of Section 2.6 of our Tenancy Agreement, which guarantees a 30-day response period. They only rescinded this demand and apologized after I formally challenged its legality.

2. Procedural Impropriety & "Secret" Adjudication
A year later, in a desperate attempt to extort money, they initiated a dispute process via HF Resolution without any notification. Under Regulation 14 of the ADR Regulations 2015, they had a statutory duty to notify me once the process commenced. Instead, they suddenly sent me a "decision" email out of nowhere, arbitrarily moving deadlines as they pleased. Their conduct was so unprofessional that I even suspected the emails were fake.

3. Suspicious and Fraudulent Evidence
When I raised issues regarding their claims, they sent me suspicious "evidence"—including photos of a completely different house that wasn't even my flat, and informal "price breakdown" files instead of proper PDF invoices. This is a level of incompetence and dishonesty that is unacceptable in a professional setting.

So, if you are a tenant, especially a foreigner or someone who might be seen as an easy target, STAY AWAY from Stirling Ackroyd. They will ignore legal procedures and contractual rights to pressure you into paying unsubstantiated amounts. This has been the most traumatic experience of my life as a tenant who has never experienced this type of unfair and non-sense dispute ever in my life.

I have now escalated this to the Ombudsman and am fully prepared for a court battle with legal representation. But anyways, please do avoid this agency if you are a foreigner. They clearly target those they perceive as easy marks.

I booked a same-day reassurance scan with Phoenix Ultrasound because I specifically wanted to see my baby’s face in 4D. Before booking, I asked whether this would actually be possible at 20 weeks, and I was told yes — although the images might not be as clear as later in pregnancy. I even asked them to check with the sonographer before confirming, and they still recommended the 4D package costing £220.

Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing.

During the scan, I was told the baby’s position was fine, yet they were still unable to capture any clear images of the baby’s face. Most of the pictures were very unclear and difficult to make out. For a service costing over £200, I expected far better image quality and overall experience.

Another major issue was that there was no second screen for parents to comfortably view the scan. I had to constantly bend my neck trying to look at the sonographer’s monitor for 20–30 minutes, which made the experience uncomfortable and frustrating.

I was also seen around 10 minutes late for my appointment.

Afterwards, I asked whether they could offer a repeat scan due to the poor images, but they refused. Instead, they only offered to downgrade the package to a reassurance scan and refund £35. They also said they would no longer provide the 4D images because of the downgrade, meaning I would only receive 2D pictures.

What made the experience even worse was that after more than 24 hours, I still had not received any report or scan results at all — whether 2D, 3D, or 4D. When I called to follow this up, I was simply told to “wait until tonight.”

To compare, I visited another ultrasound clinic shortly afterwards and received a much better experience and significantly clearer baby images, which confirmed to me that the issue was not simply due to the gestational age or baby’s position.

I have had three pregnancies and visited many ultrasound clinics over the years, and honestly this was among the worst experiences I’ve had — despite being one of the most expensive. Even at the downgraded price of £185, I do not feel the service was worth the money.

I completely understand that some imaging factors are outside the clinic’s control, but for the price charged, I expected much better communication, facilities, image quality, and customer care.

I recently had a disappointing experience travelling with Trips and Tours. The trip included a visit to Elan Valley to see the dam waterfall; however, when we arrived, it was not available to view. According to the workers there, these closures are planned in advance and visitors can be informed if enquiries are made beforehand. Unfortunately, we were never informed of this by the company.

When we raised the issue, we were told it was our responsibility to research the trip ourselves and that the dam waterfall was not explicitly advertised. However, it was heavily featured throughout the information leaflet, so naturally we expected it to be part of the experience. At no point were we advised that additional research would be necessary before booking.
The itinerary for the day also felt poorly planned. Spending around five hours in Elan Valley was excessive, especially as most coach tour companies apparently spend a shorter time there and instead take visitors around the other dams that are more easily accessible by coach or car. This was something even the workers at Elan Valley mentioned to us.

I would also like to say that the trip coordinator for the day, Hamza, was very kind, patient, and accommodating throughout the trip and genuinely tried his best to resolve any issues that arose. However, it was clear he was somewhat out of his depth due to the circumstances, which was quite sad to see, as many of the problems appeared to stem from poor planning rather than his own efforts.

The most frustrating part of the trip, however, involved two passengers who returned an hour and a half late to the coach departure time, causing everyone to worry that they were lost or in difficulty. Initially, I gave them the benefit of the doubt, but I later learned from other passengers that these same individuals have reportedly done this on multiple previous trips and that the organiser is already aware of the issue. Despite this, no apparent action has been taken, which is disappointing and unfair to the rest of the passengers who were left waiting.

Overall, the experience felt poorly organised and lacked clear communication and consideration for customers.

I have been on many trips with this company over the last few years and at one point even recommended family and friends. Over the last year I have had two notably bad experiences which were both due to bad planning and coordination from the organisers. If there was any accountability from the organisers I honestly would’ve been fine however when bought up it seemed like they didn’t care for what happened and didn’t even try to rectify the issues. Chronicles of the Yellow Containers – The Spear of Truth

The sun sank weary and pale over the smoky horizon of Brunton-Nether, like the final, guttering breath of a dying dragon. Baron S. Cardos stood in the yard of the great manufactory, his cloak torn and buffeted by the icy wind. In this realm, honor had long since been bartered away to the cold gods of steel and machine grease.

Before his feet lay the Yellow Dolavs. They were massive, dark, and looming—resembling the abandoned nests of the Dark Dragon Queen herself. They were filled with the rot of negligence, and their contents seeped out to poison the very earth.

“My Lords,” Cardos spoke, his voice ringing like cold steel upon stone within the crumbling walls of Solamnia. “The containers are filled to the brim. The order is broken. If we do not act, this darkness shall devour every soul within these walls!”

But the Council of Management only offered a mocking smile. The high chieftain of the realm, Lord Vowe Dotes, watched the events from his high tower. He was the "King," whose word was law, yet who preferred the shifting shadows to the clarity of open speech.

The Song of the Chronicles on the Great Betrayal:

The Fading of the Spring Sunlight (April 2023): The first warning cry was raised, like a distant horn blast before the coming of a storm. But the answer was not aid; it was a Deathly Silence.

The Treachery of the Summer Heat (July 2023): At last, Lord Vowe Dotes himself deigned to speak. The High Chieftain tossed a few words to the restless seeker, like a bone to a stray dog. “I have spoken to the sub-chiefs,” he etched upon the parchment, but his words were as hollow as a plundered dwarven mine.

The yellow monsters remained in the mud, bloated with the venom of irresponsibility, mocking all that was once called safety. But the Wheel of Fate turned inexorably. It was not danger, but Betrayal that finally overtook Baron S. Cardos. It was then that an ancient power awoke—a force mortals call Whistleblowing.

The cult of the Yellow Crate now performs dark rituals, trying to rewrite the past with forged runes on altered scrolls. But Baron S. Cardos knows: the truth is like Dragon-glass. Cold, sharp, and capable of slicing through even Lord Vowe Dotes’ thickest armor of lies.

The Moral:
Safety may be a discarded weapon in the hands of the weak. But the Truth is like the Dragonlance: once it finds its mark, no High Chieftain can halt the fall.

The service provided by the team was extremely disappointing and among the worst customer experiences I have encountered in a long time if not ever.

I reserved a vehicle online and paid the reservation fee, following the exact process advertised on Seat’s website: “Reserve online and we’ll mark the car as reserved for 7 days so you can finalise your order.” Based on this, any reasonable customer would expect the vehicle to be secured and unavailable for sale to anyone else.

Instead, the entire process felt disorganised and completely contradictory to what was advertised. When I was contacted the following day by the branch, there appeared to be no record of the information I had already submitted online. I was even asked to provide the vehicle registration number again over the phone, which immediately undermined confidence that the reservation had been handled correctly.

I was then told they needed to check whether the vehicle was even on site, before later being informed it was “at the back” undergoing checks. Despite this confusion, the salesperson proceeded to discuss payment terms and next steps with me, giving every impression that the vehicle had been successfully reserved and that the sale was progressing normally.

Despite this, the vehicle was seemingly placed back onto the forecourt, made available for test drives, and ultimately sold to another customer. I was later told this was down to “manager’s discretion”, which is difficult to reconcile with the reservation process clearly advertised online.

Despite numerous attempts to get clarity on the situation all afternoon, I did not receive a callback from the manager until 5:59pm.

During that call, the manager initially denied this was a “miscommunication”, and said the buyer of the vehicle was a pre-organised appointment (difficult to believe considering 4 hours earlier there was no record of the vehicle even on site) and therefore they were ‘prioritised’ over myself who reserved and followed the full process. The manager later acknowledged that this was a miscommunication…

To advertise a reservation system that supposedly secures a vehicle for seven days, only for that vehicle to then be sold to somebody else while the original customer is actively progressing the purchase, is extremely disappointing, amateurish and far below the standard you expect from an authorised Seat dealer.

The UK Brand Myth: I paid a significant premium for these locks because I wanted to support a UK business and have the peace of mind of London-based support. It was a massive mistake. Simpled is a corporate facade operating out of a WeWork address, selling fragile hardware with a support system designed to stall and frustrate.

Pricing Chaos: There is zero consistency in their pricing. They list these locks at £169 on their website, sometimes discounted to £99, while charging £139 on Amazon. It is a blatant attempt to see how much they can squeeze out of you.

The Hardware Saga: I ordered three units initially. One arrived with a broken front panel. Despite the heavy price tag, this isn't some bespoke system. The locks run entirely on a basic, third-party app (TTLock). Worse yet, the core biometric feature is practically useless; the fingerprint sensor is so unreliable that the lock mostly wouldn't open even after 8 to 10 attempts. The replacement I eventually received for the broken unit appeared to be a used customer return and was just as defective.

The Most Ridiculous Part: When I had to replace another faulty component, the shipping took a full week. To make matters worse, they had the audacity to blame me for a part that broke while I was simply trying to fix their defective hardware. They then tried to charge me an extra £33 for the replacement part. I was only in that position because their original product was faulty, yet they tried to turn it into a profit-making opportunity.

The Support Nightmare: They boast about UK resident support, yet it routinely took them 24 hours or more to reply to a basic email. I spent a week in an exhausting loop of stalling tactics. Even after management admitted they got many things wrong, they suggested a resolution with an offer I didn't even ask for. Given the days of physical labor and the sheer administrative hassle they caused, the offer was quite frankly insulting anyway!

The Truth: I have since ripped these out and replaced them with alternative locks that cost only £40. To be honest, the £40 replacements are far superior in every way. The biometrics work instantly and the build quality puts Simpled to shame.

The Verdict: Save your money, your time, and your doors. You can buy a better product for £40 elsewhere and avoid the headache of a company that cares more about its image than its customers.

It is up to you to make your own mind up, but I have done the legwork so you don't have to.

UPDATE: The owner has replied below attempting to blame an "inexperienced team member." This is completely false. It was their Customer Service Manager who offered me an insulting token gesture after a week of stalling. Now they are suggesting I should have left a voicemail, despite them taking 24 plus hours to reply to basic emails.

Blaming your staff and even your customers instead of taking responsibility tells you everything you need to know about this company.

I feel like the Guild of Students sometimes buries its head in the sand. Deleting comments or blocking people simply because they don’t like what’s being said isn’t what a student guild should stand for. It should be a space where all voices are heard. If people raise concerns, those should be addressed openly rather than silenced.

For example, I commented that it’s concerning how few home students have been standing for roles recently, and that this is something worth looking into—especially given that the last two elections have shown the same pattern. Instead of responding or acknowledging the concern, my comment was simply deleted. That kind of approach comes across as dismissive and poor.

If students are offering valid feedback—whether on social media or any other platform—it should be taken seriously. The Guild should ensure students feel heard and represented, especially on issues they care strongly about. Personally, I feel there’s a growing lack of representation for home students in these roles. While it’s important to have positions like an international officer for international student issues, there should also be stronger representation for home students.

There used to be a much broader and more diverse range of candidates, but now it feels like that balance has shifted. It’s important that home students still feel encouraged and supported to get involved, rather than feeling like these opportunities aren’t really for them anymore.

Title: £300 a year lost for being a loyal customer

As a long-standing customer with a substantial savings balance, I was very disappointed to discover I am receiving a significantly lower interest rate than what is currently offered to new customers on similar accounts.

This is not a small difference — it equates to hundreds of pounds per year in lost interest.

I raised this as a formal complaint, but the response did not explain why existing customers are left on lower rates or offer any meaningful solution. There is also no clear or proactive way to ensure customers are moved to more competitive rates.

I understand banks offer incentives to attract new customers, but this feels like a clear loyalty penalty. Existing customers should not be disadvantaged in this way.

Very disappointing experience.

I’m disappointed that Monument is offering 4.51% to new savers while existing long-term customers are left on a much lower rate of 3.77%.

That gap feels unfair, especially when you require a minimum balance of £25k, because the savings are substantial and the difference in interest really adds up over time.

I raised this concern and the reply was polite, but it did not properly address why loyal customers are left behind or offer a clear solution.

A bank that wants trust from savers should treat existing customers fairly as well as new ones.
