one_star_reviews.text: Communication from block management is atrocious, expect no reply and constant chasing up.

My previous review highlighted the lack of cleaning in communal areas, FIRE DOORS that DON’T CLOSE, broken light fittings and window fittings that don’t match, never ending extra charges and TERRIBLE communication.

Your response? You, are “happy” with the cleaning company hired by you on our behalf. No response to anything else. No change.

UPDATE 3

After months of reporting concerns about the communal cleaning in my building, I finally spoke directly today with the cleaner responsible for my area.

What concerns me most is that the conversation raised further inconsistencies with the repeated assurances I had previously been given by management that “no issues” had been identified and that the area had been cleaned satisfactorily.

Despite repeatedly providing timestamped and geolocated photographs over several months, my complaint was ultimately dismissed and closed down by Martin Nicholls without any meaningful engagement with the specific evidence I had raised regarding the area outside my flat.

Communication throughout this process has been extremely poor. I have repeatedly had to chase responses, received little meaningful follow-up, and despite public responses stating the matter had been escalated, I was not properly contacted regarding the concerns I had continued raising all year.

During today’s interaction, the cleaner confirmed:
- my doormat is not moved during cleaning,
- the area is instead cleaned “around” the mat,
- and a completely new explanation was introduced that the electrical outlet near my flat allegedly does not work, affecting the ability to vacuum the area properly.

The cleaner then asked to use my own electrical outlet in order to vacuum the area.

This immediately raises the obvious question of how the area outside my flat was supposedly being vacuumed previously while I was repeatedly being assured over several months that the area had been cleaned and inspected properly.

For clarity, my complaint has always related specifically to the area immediately outside my flat. However, the wider condition of the building and communal areas also raises obvious concerns regarding the overall standard and consistency of cleaning being carried out across the site.

At this stage, I honestly do not know what service leaseholders are actually paying for. From what I now understand, it appears that one cleaner may effectively be responsible for multiple blocks and large communal areas. If that is the case, I do not place personal blame on the cleaner herself. My concern is with the management and oversight of the service being provided, the standard being accepted, and the repeated dismissal of feedback and evidence raised throughout the year.

I have now retained recordings, photographs and a full correspondence timeline and will be referring the matter to the Property Redress Scheme for independent review.

At this stage, my concern is no longer just the standard of cleaning itself, but the repeated contradiction between what has been communicated to leaseholders and what the evidence continues to show.

West Midlands Airsoft was once a welcoming site that encouraged conversation, sportsmanship, and a good atmosphere between players, which makes my recent experience especially disappointing.

From the start of the day, the atmosphere felt uncomfortable and unwelcoming. The marshal team came across as cliquey and noticeably more engaged with regular players, while newer or less familiar faces felt overlooked. Unfortunately, this created an environment that felt difficult to settle into rather than one that encouraged players to get involved and enjoy the hobby.

The safety briefing also felt unnecessarily aggressive in tone. A phrase along the lines of “pack your bags and leave, we don’t want you here” was repeated multiple times throughout the briefing. While safety standards and rule enforcement are obviously important in airsoft, the delivery felt more threatening than constructive and set a negative tone for the day before games had even begun.

Throughout the event, there also appeared to be a culture of aggressive cheating accusations among some players, which seemed to reflect the wider atmosphere on site. Rather than disputes being handled calmly and constructively, interactions often felt confrontational, making the experience uncomfortable.

From a gameplay perspective, the map design was disappointing. Several layouts encouraged bottlenecks and linear engagements, leading to stagnant gameplay with limited tactical variation. Across game modes, positioning and flow felt repetitive, which reduced variety over the course of the day.

It also feels as though the site’s focus has shifted. The retail side appears to have been prioritised, with pricing feeling noticeably high, while the community-focused atmosphere that once made the site enjoyable seems to have diminished.

It’s unfortunate to see what was once a friendly and welcoming environment feel so different. Leadership and site culture inevitably shape player behaviour, and from my experience there seems to have been a noticeable change in tone that has filtered through the marshal team and wider player base.

Based on my experiences, I would struggle to recommend visiting at this time. I hope feedback like this is taken constructively, as the site clearly has potential and I would genuinely like to see it return to the welcoming environment it once was

We spent three years in the UK going through infertility with no known cause, no previous children, both healthy, and even with top‑grade embryos and expensive treatments like PGT‑A, nothing worked. We invested thousands and were repeatedly told everything looked “normal,” yet we were left without answers or solutions. It was only after our last embryo failed that we went abroad, completely exhausted and desperate for something different. Within a short time, they carried out a simple HSG dye test—which also has a therapeutic flushing effect and is standard practice there but not routinely offered in the UK. That test immediately showed a structural issue with my partner’s uterus, and they followed up with a minor procedure that is far more tightly restricted under UK practice. The result? Within a month we conceived naturally, and our baby was born healthy at 39 weeks. The doctor abroad even predicted complications with delivery based on the uterine shape—which turned out to be accurate with an eventual C‑section. It’s incredibly frustrating to look back and realise that this wasn’t about a lack of medical knowledge, but about how the system is run. In simple terms, the UK and parts of Europe approach uterine septum very differently because they interpret the same evidence in different ways. NICE guidance in the UK acknowledges that a septum can be linked to fertility problems, but says the direct cause isn’t clearly proven, so doctors are cautious and tend to avoid surgery unless there’s strong evidence—often after repeated losses or failures. In contrast, many European (ESHRE‑style) clinics accept that uncertainty but take a more practical, patient‑focused approach: even if it’s not definitively proven, a septum may affect implantation or pregnancy outcomes, and removing it is a relatively straightforward, low‑risk procedure, so they act on it earlier. From a patient perspective, it’s hard not to feel that the UK approach focuses too heavily on limiting intervention rather than fully exploring possible causes—especially when the outcome of taking action elsewhere led directly to the child we now have. This practice offered us £0 in compensation.

I rarely leave reviews, but after my experience with this teaching agency, I feel compelled to share my honest opinion so that other educators can make informed decisions.

I registered with this agency in September 2025, and from then until May 2026, I received only around seven days of work in total. On several occasions, bookings were cancelled at the very last minute, causing unnecessary inconvenience and instability.

In my experience, the agency did not operate with professionalism, fairness, or transparency. Concerns I raised regarding unsuitable school placements and overall treatment were repeatedly dismissed. Instead of addressing legitimate issues, I was often told that “work had been offered and refused,” without any acknowledgement of the serious concerns I had raised about certain placements.

What I found particularly disappointing was the lack of support and safeguarding for teachers’ welfare and professional reputation. Negative feedback was allegedly received from certain schools, yet no clear explanation, evidence, or constructive discussion was ever provided. As an experienced educator with more than 25 years of teaching experience across both the UK and international prestigious institutions, I found this deeply unfair and unprofessional—especially considering the strong references and positive track record I have built throughout my career.

Sadly, this was not my first negative experience with the agency. Over 12 years ago, during a previous registration under different staff management, I experienced what I can only describe as low grade childish allegation that was uninvestigated, unfair treatment and collusion with a particular school and teaching personnel. At that time, concerns were raised against me without proper investigation, resulting in my removal from the agency in a heartless, damaging manner including their interference with another agency I was working with that i was laid off simultaneously on this false allegation. Given the difficult personal circumstances I was facing at the time, the experience was extremely damaging to my career and wellbeing.

After more than a decade, I genuinely believed the agency would have evolved and improved. Unfortunately, I found many of the same issues still present, the same childish but adult calculating minds for the damage of teachers careers which left me feeling deeply disappointed for trusting them a second time.

I recently informed Molly that I no longer wished to continue working with the agency due to the lack of sufficient work and the overall experience. Unfortunately, there was little effort made to resolve matters professionally or restore confidence. Similar concerns apply to my interactions with Megan Ryder and Michael.

It is important to note that teachers undergo rigorous vetting, safeguarding checks, and professional scrutiny before being accepted by agencies. For this reason, educators deserve to be treated with fairness, dignity, transparency, and respect.

Inspite of many positive reviews regarding how brilliant teaching personnel are, I personally find this very difficult to believe. They bad mouth and collude with schools to damage teachers.

One has to remember that the recruitment staff play a fundamental role in giving any agency its good or bad image. However, I don't know what staff the review writers on here were actually dealing with. I find it impossible as an highly educated and critic individual that so many positive reviews have been left on here. I hope that people can open up a little more and be factual in what they write.

I encourage others to share their honest experiences as well. Constructive criticism can sometimes encourage organisations to reflect, improve, and treat their staff more ethically and professionally in the future.
I am glad to see the back of them and will never look back at them.

Misleading lead in times. I ordered window shutters from Just Blinds in November 2025. At that time the company gave a lead in time for the order of 12 to 14 weeks. Today I received an update to state that there is a further delay of 2 months where the shipment is not due to arrive in the UK until April. That’s a total of 6 months between order and potential installation. I wrote back to the company explaining my dissatisfaction with the delay and asked what compensation they were willing to offer as a result of the delay. I then received a curt and abrupt response saying they do not provide compensation pointing out the small print of their terms and conditions which state that if delivery is delayed by their supplier they are entitled to a reasonable delay. I do not consider 2 months a reasonable delay! What the company don’t highlight when you make your order is that their shutters are sourced from China. Be aware of this company not being willing to be reasonable in offering any type of compensation if things go wrong and anticipate that the original lead in times given are misleading at the very least!!! My message to Just Blinds is you have one very dissatisfied customer and the very least you should be doing is offering some form of compensation together with recognising your quoted lead in times are misleading, a 2 month delay is not ok or reasonable! Ask yourself this question if a customer ordered shutters today are you going to tell them that the best you can do for them is an instillation in 6 months time???
Review update 10/03/26 Following my original review, the company responded publicly and suggested they would offer a goodwill gesture to address the situation. Unfortunately, despite that response & even after emailing the owner of the company directly nothing has actually been followed through or provided.

At this point it appears the response was more about managing the optics of the review than genuinely resolving the issue. The original problem involved significant delays and misleading timelines, and the promised goodwill gesture now seems like a cynical attempt to deflect criticism rather than a sincere effort to put things right.

Review update 30/03/25
Further update to my original review — and somehow, this situation continues to get worse.

I was contacted today by the company to be informed that my already delayed shutters order (placed in November 2025) is now facing yet another delay. I am now being told that the shipment from China may not even dock until the end of April, making it highly unlikely that installation will take place before May 2026 — approximately six months after the order was placed.

Let’s not forget: the original estimated lead time provided by this company was 12–14 weeks.

Delays can happen — that’s not the real issue here. What truly stands out is the complete lack of accountability and the apparent disdain for customers when things go wrong.

I emailed Clair Gill on 5th March asking for clarification regarding the so-called “goodwill gesture” that was publicly mentioned in response to my original review. To date, I have received no reply whatsoever. During today’s call, the staff member I spoke to was also unable — or unwilling — to confirm what this gesture actually is.

The only logical conclusion is that this “goodwill gesture” exists purely as a public relations statement on Google, rather than a genuine attempt to resolve the issue.

To anyone considering using this company: be extremely cautious. Based on my experience, they cannot be trusted with your money. The owner has demonstrated a complete unwillingness to engage directly with customers when problems arise, and not even the basic courtesy of responding to emails.

I genuinely feel sorry for the staff, who are left to deal with frustrated customers and attempt to defend what is, quite frankly, unacceptable customer service driven from the top.

I purchased six white gloss cubicles from Gary for installation in my sunbed salon at a cost of over £7,000. Initially, communication was very positive, and Gary attended the premises to measure and sketch the layout in order to secure the work. Although I had seen some negative reviews online, I chose to proceed as he is a local supplier and I wanted to support a nearby business.

Gary originally confirmed the cubicles would be installed one week before our opening date, however this was later delayed, which resulted in us having to postpone our salon opening.

On the day of installation, Gary did not attend himself and instead sent a subcontractor to complete the work. At first glance the cubicles appeared acceptable, but once we began preparing the salon for opening it became clear that none of the doors were properly aligned, leaving large gaps which are not appropriate for private changing cubicles. In addition, the locks were incorrectly fitted and misaligned, meaning several doors were difficult to secure and some could not be locked at all.

Since installation, I have made multiple attempts over the past five months to resolve these issues directly with Gary. Unfortunately, visits have either been cancelled or ignored altogether. To date, the faults remain unresolved and no repairs or refunds have been offered.

This situation has been extremely disappointing and unprofessional, particularly given the cost of the installation and the impact on my business. I regret not taking the earlier reviews more seriously.

I took out a premium SMART repair and alloy wheel insurance policy, expecting straightforward cover for minor cosmetic damage. Just six weeks in, I scuffed the front lower lip of my car and submitted a claim with clear photos and a full explanation.

The claim was declined on the basis that the part was “not factory painted.” This was incorrect. The lower lip is factory finished, and I had simply applied a protective wrap to help prevent stone chips. I made it clear that the wrap could be removed prior to any repair, so it had no bearing on the validity of the claim.

Despite providing this clarification, the process became unnecessarily drawn out. Responses were slow, and the decision did not change. It felt less like a genuine assessment and more like an attempt to avoid liability.

I eventually cancelled the policy, but only received a partial refund, which added further frustration given how early into the term this occurred.

What makes this more disappointing is that I previously worked in the motor trade and sold a significant number of these policies, including those under Premia Solutions. I have seen first hand how they should operate and have supported many customers through successful claims. Based on this experience, the handling of this case falls well below expectations.

My overall impression is that there is a clear reluctance to approve claims and a similar resistance when it comes to issuing fair refunds. The product may sound comprehensive at point of sale, but the real test is how claims are handled, and in this instance, it did not deliver.

I had a very poor experience with BCA, Perry Bar.

I purchased a vehicle listed as a 2025 plate with 20,000 miles, graded as a Grade 3. Based on that grading and the listing, I travelled 2.5 hours to collect the car - only to find that it wouldn’t even start on arrival. On closer inspection, there was also significant damage that had not been clearly photographed or properly described in the listing.

When I raised this with staff on site, I was passed to a case manager, Wasim. Unfortunately, the experience only worsened from there. He was dismissive and repeatedly stated he was “doing me a favour” by even supporting the case. He maintained that the vehicle had been graded correctly and offered only a minimal goodwill gesture, claiming there was nothing more he could do.

After two weeks of back and forth, I was told again that the grading was correct and that he had personally driven the vehicle. Delivery was then arranged as part of the goodwill gesture.

However, concerned by the lack of formal confirmation, I contacted head office directly. I was then informed that the vehicle had in fact been incorrectly graded, and that the correct appraisal had not been uploaded to the system. Despite this, delivery had already been arranged-seemingly on the basis that I had accepted a goodwill gesture.

This raises serious concerns about transparency and intent. It felt as though the situation was being handled in a way that encouraged me to accept the vehicle despite known issues.

Only after escalating the matter further to a regional manager was I offered a full refund.

Overall, this was a frustrating and time-wasting experience. Travelling several hours to collect a misrepresented vehicle, followed by poor communication and dismissive handling, is not acceptable. I would strongly advise others to exercise caution-particularly when dealing with case management and their in-house grading process.

I visited this salon after a recommendation and, while the staff were friendly and polite, I was hoping for a good experience. Unfortunately, this was the worst hair experience I have had.

I had an appointment with a stylist called Sercia (apologies if I’ve misspelled her name). I don’t like naming individuals, but I feel it’s important so others can be cautious and as a learning point for ensuring clients’ requests are properly followed. And for the stylist to ask and listen and fillow what clients have asked for.
I asked for a slight trim as I have long hair, and for my bangs to be freshened up, as it had grown down to my neck so just a trim above my chin would have been great. Instead, my bangs was cut much shorter than requested using thinning scissors, and cut in a way that made it obvious too much had been taken off.

My hair was long lenght and  thick so i asked for a trim to freshen it up. My hair was thinned from the front, and the back too badly, and throughout—something I did not ask for at all. I specifically requested a small trim, not for my hair to be thinned.

Before the appointment, I explained that I already have anxiety around getting my hair done. I was reassured by the stylist, who said she understood as she had experieced similar feelings herself. That’s why it’s especially upsetting that my requests were not followed.

At the start, I was told it would only be a small trim because my hair is long. However, after the cut was already done, a bouncy blow-dry was suggested when this wasnt recommended for my hair length at beginning. By that point, I couldn’t properly see what had been done until it was too late.

I had spent years growing my hair to the thickness and length I wanted, so this has been genuinely distressing and has affected my confidence. Even my work colleagues immediately noticed how much my hair had been thinned.

I don’t understand why my wishes weren’t respected, especially after I explained them clearly. Everyone’s experience may differ, but unfortunately this has really affected me, and I would not return.

I had a car accident on the 15/05/19 when another driver drove straight into the back of me on the motorway. She accepted full responsibility so it was sent to Gemini Dudley to be repaired.
Car picked up fine and took them 3 weeks to repair it and redeliver it back to me. They told me that my insurance had written it off as it was too much to repair. This meant that I started looking for another car. Nearly signed a new finance deal with a garage, and just decided to check how much my insurance would pay out. My insurance had no idea what I was talking about and told me that it was in the process of being repaired. If I hadn't checked I would have ended up with a £15,000 finance car I needed to pay.
The second I got in to drive it,  my dashboard lit up like a Christmas tree. Check engine light, service lights the lot came on. Rang the garage and was told that someone would bring a diagnostic computer out tomorrow morning and plug it in.
Went to the shops, opened my boot to put my shopping in, and the whole boot floor fell down into my spare wheel compartment. They hadn't even attached my car boot floor back to my car and literally just placed it on! I'm thankful it was just a bag of shopping and not a my 2 dogs that usually sit in there.
Decided to check over the rest of the car. FILTHY interior, shoe prints on my back seats. Car is covered in scratches (I had 2 scratches on my car when it went into to be repaired, it came back with over 20!). A/C button broken, upholstery peeled off my gear stick, rear bumper wasn't even attached to my car! They then told me that they never even touched my boot? The impact was on the rear of my car and therefore the boot. The whole boot door was replaced, yet apparently they didn't even touch it? So it magically fixed itself apparently.

I get my car back the next day and the bumper has been put back on. The boot floor has been reattached etc.  I thought everything was good. Then 2 days later I opened the passenger door for the first time and notice all various car parts in the passenger door! These were definitely not there when it went in. So again, I contact the garage to explain and demand an explanation.
I speak to Leon, to which he replies. "We haven't done any work on that car. It went from your house to Renault and we haven't touched it". Yet the day before, he admitted that THEY had fixed the imperfections. I have date stamps, and also video recording and CCTV of it leaving my possession broken and coming back fixed. But apparently they didn't do any work to it. So again, my car has magically fixed itself.
I ask where all the grommets and car parts in my door have come from to which Leon laughs and replies "So you've had a lot for work done for free and you're complaining?"
Are you joking? You had no reason to be rifling about and taking my draining system at the front of my car apart. And yes I am complaining about "free work". Especially when you cant even be bothered to put it together correctly. I suppose I could pull all the wallpaper off your house and I could repaint only half? Don't you dare moan! After all, you've had half a job done for free. Shame the other half is a complete mess eh? You should be grateful for free work.

I have now started the report to trading standards, financial ombudsman and motoring ombudsman. I have timestamped photos, reports from the garage signed by their mechanics. All emails, phone calls, CCTV and video recordings as evidence.
I have been given money from my insurance to go elsewhere. That in itself speaks for itself. Insurance companies don't cough up cash easily without evidence of complete incompetence on the garage's behalf.
AVOID these monkeys like the plague. I would have been better off having my car written off then the absolute farce this garage has caused the last 2 months (and still ongoing).

Update: The car had to be sent to another garage as they had stuck my rear bumper on with DOUBLE SIDED STICKY TAPE and a SINGLE SCREW!! My insurance have had to raise a claim with the garage to get the money back. Absolute shambles!

one_star_reviews.text:
England values politeness in business relationships, which is commendable. Sadly, I’m forced to be frank and impolite in order to tell the truth about my experience with a property I rented through Marsh and Parsons. This is my first time I have every made a public comment, and it pains me to do so. To foreigners planning to rent in London—I would strongly advise proceeding with extreme caution when engaging the Notting Hill office of Marsh and Parsons and the landlords they represent.
When I began my tenancy, it was clear after a few hours that something was very “off” with the property. Poor professional cleaning: hair in shower, dirty dishes piled up, dirt on the floor, stained and worn out old sheets and towels. Of greater concern was a waste pipe covered with human sewage leaking into the wall of the bedroom and causing a mold and damp outbreak in the cupboard, which created tennis ball-sized holes in the walls and buckled the cabinetry. You could smell the sewage and mold when you entered the flat and whoever slept there was inhaling spores during the night. Wallpaper filled with damp and mildew. A bathroom ventilator fan filled with black mold. Sewage smells from the shower drain. The property neglect and deferred maintenance was endless. It was startling to find this in a flat I rented for just under 7,000 GBP per month.
Marsh and Parsons at first took the landlord’s side, saying they’d never had problems with the property before and intimating I had no right to end the tenancy.  I entered into a legal dispute with the landlord, which required me to navigate the UK legal system, hire a solicitor, plus mold and water inspectors.
In the pre-signing negotiations, the agent I worked with took the side of the landlord in every instance, refusing to negotiate a different start date, refusing basic requests like window washing, and when I asked for a normal 6 month break clause, claimed they were unheard of, which was false as I knew other agents offered those. The agent didn’t inform me the holding deposit was non-refundable and only informed me after I had transferred it. As a foreigner renting in London for the first time, I expected greater transparency and information on the part of my “advocate” in the process.
To European and American renters and others seeking a clean, safe home in London—in my experience, Marsh and Parsons offers no quality control over the properties they promote and takes the side of the landlord over the tenant in every instance including gray areas subject to negotiation as well as financial issues. Basic standards of property maintenance and client relations you are accustomed to at home are unlikely to be on display here. The managing director of the Notting Hill office is kind and professional, but ineffectual. The landlord I dealt with masquerades as a “professional” landlord, but only takes action when threatened with legal action or when served with legal papers. I am at a loss for words.

one_star_reviews.text:
Visited for breakfast with a friend recently and unfortunately left very disappointed with both the service and the way a simple issue was handled.

I ordered a breakfast which included toast. When it arrived, the toast had already been buttered. However, this was not stated anywhere on the menu, nor was it mentioned by staff when the order was taken. I do not eat butter, so I politely raised this with the staff member.

Rather than resolving the issue professionally, I was told that it was my fault because I “should have known” and should have specifically requested no butter. I explained that if this is standard practice, it should either be clearly stated on the menu or communicated when ordering. I regularly eat breakfast at cafés and restaurants around the city and across the country, and in most places staff will either mention that the toast comes buttered or serve the butter separately.

What was most disappointing was the response and attitude from staff. I was told that “99% of customers are happy with butter,” which may well be true, but good customer service is about understanding that there will always be the 1% who may have different dietary preferences or requirements. Situations like this should be handled with professionalism and understanding, not by blaming the customer or creating an argument over something so minor.

To put it into perspective, if a loaf of bread costs around £1.50 and contains approximately 20 slices, that works out at around 7.5p per slice. The two replacement slices of toast would therefore have cost roughly 15p for the Cafe. This was never about the money or being charged, it was the principle of the situation and the unnecessary rudeness and attitude shown instead of simply resolving the issue politely.

The interaction left both myself and my friend feeling uncomfortable to the point we decided to leave our meals and walk out entirely.

I would strongly encourage management to review staff training, particularly in relation to customer communication, professionalism, and handling minor issues appropriately. It would also help to amend the menu descriptions or ensure staff inform customers beforehand when items such as toast are served buttered by default.

Small issues do not become bad experiences because of the mistake itself, but because of how they are handled.

one_star_reviews.text: FBC are useless. 7 years later and they're still unable to administer my mother's estate despite receiving probate some years ago. Their responses are slow and in some instances non existent, I wholeheartedly cannot recommend.

Unfortunately, we used FBC Manby Bowdler when purchasing our first home in 2020, initially attracted by their competitive quote. However, our experience was frustrating from the start. Our main contact often seemed unaware of the progress of our case, rarely responded to emails, and was difficult to reach by phone. At one point, we even visited in person as the chain was being delayed due to a lack of progress on our side. What should have been a straightforward process ended up taking three months.

I am writing this review now because, unfortunately, we had to deal with them again during our recent move, as they were acting for our seller. The same issues arose, poor communication and delays. Both our solicitor and the seller’s estate agent repeatedly had to chase them for updates, and our buyer was even threatening to pull out due to the lack of progress.

On the day of completion, the situation became extremely stressful. FBC had not released the funds, leaving us stuck in limbo with removal vans waiting. We drove to the seller’s estate agent to try to speed things up and waited there from 12pm while attempting to contact the seller’s solicitor. We were told she was on her lunch break, so we waited even longer while costs continued to rise. When we called back, we were told by a colleague to stop calling.

We finally received the keys at 3pm and didn’t finish moving into our new home until 9pm.

In future, I will be checking which solicitor the seller is using, and will be very cautious if it is FBC Manby Bowdler.

Not impressed. I was enrolled with Embark through Barclays Wealth Management pension scheme and therefore anticipated a premium service.
Due to an unexpected change in my financial circumstances I needed to access my retirement funds at short notice.
Embark required a document of around 16-17 pages completing. A physical copy of the document then had to be posted to Embark. Embark then had a target of 11 working days to respond, which meant that each iteration required around 3 working weeks to complete at a time in my life where every day counted.
Once completed successfully I kept a copy of the successful documentation for future reference.
When I did require further funds I completed a new form based on the previous successful document only to find that the format of the document had changed with no notification to myself and I had to start again from scratch.
Barclays were willing to assist me in completing the forms successfully but for a fee of 1% of my total pension fund. Ultimately I was able to complete the form successfully at my first attempt after about an hour's work.
I ultimately transferred away from Embark to another company that only required an email from myself to make changes to my financial arrangements and typically implemented the changes successfully within a matter of days.
I understand that Embark have subsequently joined the 21st Century and will now accept the forms via email.
Their phone service was acceptable, providing me with updates as required when I rang them, rather than having to await the full 11 days plus postal time turnaround, hence the 1 star, as I would othewise have tried to give them zero stars.
They took a point in my life that was incredibly stressful and made it much worse, they seem to run the service to their own antiquated desires, rather than their clients requirements.
It is now mid May and have received my P60 for the previous financial year from the firm I swithched to, but am still awaiting my P60 for my previous year's pension from Embark.

If only you could give zero stars… the worst landlords we have dealt with in London.

We had an extremely disappointing experience with The Bedford Estates and would strongly caution anyone considering renting through them.

At the end of our tenancy, they attempted to deduct nearly £3,000 from our deposit for what can only be described as routine wear and tear after a two-year tenancy. This included full redecoration of multiple rooms, minor scuffs, ageing silicone, and trivial items such as removable tape, none of which reasonably justify the level of charges being proposed.

What was particularly concerning was that these deductions were issued before the check-out report was even provided. When the report was eventually shared, it actually contradicted many of the claims, categorising the majority of items as fair wear and tear or minor issues.

We also agreed to use their nominated cleaners (at their quoted price) to avoid any disputes at check-out, yet they still attempted to raise further cleaning-related issues afterwards. This felt both unreasonable and inconsistent.

In addition, they refused to provide even a basic factual reference for our onward tenancy, citing the service of a Section 21 notice (which is a no-fault eviction). This was both unhelpful and, frankly, demonstrated a lack of understanding of standard practice.

Separately, our personal details were shared with third-party marketing agents before we were formally notified in writing, which raised concerns around how our data was handled.

Throughout the process, communication was slow, unhelpful, and at times dismissive. The overall handling gave the impression of an attempt to pass refurbishment costs onto tenants rather than applying a fair and proportionate assessment.

For context, we have rented in London for over 10 years and have always had our deposits returned without issue. This experience was by far the worst we have encountered.

We are now forced to go through the deposit adjudication process to recover what should have been returned in the first place.

Proceed with caution. In fact, run the other way.
